messages.subject: mapPies
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
 I work on allelic frequency and  I'm using the function mapPies of package " rworlmap" . I would like to reduce (1) the size of my piechart and (2) add the number of each population  next to them and I can not do it. This is the code that I use:

mapPies(data,nameX="LON",nameY="LAT",nameZs=c("allele1","allele2",
"allele3","allele4","allele5","allele6","allele7","allele8","allele9",
"allele10","allele11","allele12","allele13","allele14","allele15"),
zColours=c("black","red","blue","yellow","green","blueviolet","gray","cyan","firebrick","floralwhite","gold","red4","magenta","hotpink","burlywood4"), symbolMaxSize=0.5, ratio = 1, xlim= c(-20,35), ylim= c(40,65), borderCol = "black", lwd = 3)

Here is the link of my map

https://www.dropbox.com/s/8dp741z5kwxw08q/pietest.pptx

Thank in advance for your help.
Mireille

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] mapPies
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mireille,

1) to change the size of pies try setting symbolSize=0.5 (not symbolMaxSize)
2) You could try something like :
text(data$LON, data$LAT, labels=data$[insert name of your column], pos=1, offset=-2)
and play with offset & pos to get the labels in a position you like.

Best wishes,
Andy

Hello Andy et al.,

When joining country data to a map (joinCountryData2Map()) I get the following report back:

"225 codes from your data successfully matched countries in the map
2 codes from your data failed to match with a country code in the map
29 codes from the map weren't represented in your data"

How can I easily determine the countries that failed to match and the missing countries?

Many thanks,

--

Best wishes,
Andy

messages.subject: Number of successes/failures when data are joined to a map
messages.subject_clean: Number of successes/failures when data are joined to a map
messages.body_plain:
When the command joinCountryData2Map is used, it outputs a nice message indicating the number of country codes that matched countries in the map successfully.

However, it would be nice to get this number of successes in a variable that can be used in the code so that it doesn't have to be hard-coded into a script after having applied the function. The object that is returned by this function is pretty complex so I haven't been able to find if it contains this number in it.

Does anyone know how to retrieve from this object (or even if it exists there at all)?

Thanks in advance!

messages.subject: Re: Number of successes/failures when data are joined to a map
messages.subject_clean: Number of successes/failures when data are joined to a map
messages.body_plain:
Good question Juan ! Thanks.

The reproducible example below shows how you can get the number of successful & failed joins relatively easily.

If there was a call for this it occurs to me I could return a list with these numbers and the country names, but it would have to be returned instead of the map. I could do it in one of 2 ways.

1) adding an argument something like checkMode=TRUE to joinCountryData2Map
2) creating a new function, but can't think what  would call it without name length getting (more) excessive.

Any comments anyone ?

Thanks,
Andy

library(rworldmap)

#create test data
dF <- data.frame( country=c("spain", "uk", "notacountry")
                , weather=c("hot", "cold", "neither") )

#join to map
sPDF <- joinCountryData2Map( dF
                       , joinCode = "NAME"
                       , nameJoinColumn = "country" )

#to get the number of matches check one of the column names from your
#original data and find how many non-NAs there are
numMatchedCountries <- length( which( !is.na <http://is.na>(sPDF$weather) ) )
#[1] 2
numFailures <- nrow(dF) - numMatchedCountries
#[1] 1
